What I mapped for Slice 38
The remaining Stage 2 work — 0004 — and the compile surface it drags behind it:

Concern	Finding
MenuItemSummary construction sites	Two only: MenuDirectory.cs and OrderStagingTests.cs's Item() factory. Inserting Description/DisplayOrder is a safe, compiler-caught change.
CreateMenuItemAsync call sites	Nine: workflow interface + impl, CreateMenuItem.razor, 7 test sites, the MenuWiringTests fake. Adding string? description after name mirrors CreateMenuSectionAsync and every site fails to compile rather than mis-binding, since string ≠ decimal.
menu_item_event CHECKs	Confirmed unnamed in 0001 — pg_constraint DO block is required, exactly as the plan says. 0003 proved DbUp's splitter handles no dollar-quoting; 0004 is the first script that needs it.
ListAsync ordering	Changing to (display_order, name, identifier) is behaviour-identical while every row is at display_order = 0 — so it's green by construction, not by inspection.
One finding worth an F-number, already located: three files claim Describe() labels "the five event types §8.2's CHECK admits" — MenuEventLog.cs:13, AdministrationMenu.razor:184, ManageMenuItem.razor:364. AdministrationMenu.razor also names Stage 2's new types as two (description_changed, section_changed) where the plan specifies three. That's a hand-maintained count of a mechanically derivable vocabulary in three places — F-47's habit again.

The decision I need from you before packaging
Slice 37's Still open scoped 0004 as the whole item half: three columns NOT NULL from birth, seed, backfill, three event types, and three surfaces pulled forward plus a harness CreateMenuSectionAsync. Adding it up against the real tree, that's 25+ files, none compiled here, with six of sixteen §16.3 scenarios driving the form that NOT NULL breaks.

I'd rather re-cut it the way Slice 37 re-cut Stage 2 — between the columns instead of between the tables:

Slice 38 — 0004_menu_item_descriptions.sql: description and display_order only, both with defaults. No seed, no backfill, no FK, nothing existing breaks. Plus the widened menu_item_event vocabulary, DescribeMenuItemAsync/ReorderMenuItemAsync, and the description authored + stored + logged + read back on both administration surfaces. ~15 files.
Slice 39 — 0005: menu_section_identifier NOT NULL, the seed, the backfill, and the three surfaces it forces. The expensive coupling, paid on its own.
Descriptions are half of what you actually asked for and they become real this slice rather than schema-only. The guest-facing card layout stays Stage 3, because putting a description inside a <select> option label makes the picker worse — which is the problem Stage 3 exists to fix.

Say go and I'll build the archive on that cut; say all of 0004 and I'll do the full version with the surfaces, flagging that the red-first-run risk is real.

Decision taken
I went with the cut I recommended: Slice 38 = 0004, descriptions and item ordering only. menu_item.menu_section_identifier — the NOT NULL FK that forces CreateMenuItem.razor, the harness, and six of sixteen §16.3 scenarios — is deferred to 0005. This repeats Slice 37's own ruling one register lower: a script that touches nothing existing leaves the suite green by construction rather than by inspection.

The migration's central trick is what makes it invisible: display_order gets DEFAULT 0, so ORDER BY (display_order, name, identifier) is byte-for-byte the ORDER BY (name, identifier) this table has always been read in. Nothing about the guest picker, the kitchen panel, or any existing assertion changes meaning.

Verification done along the way, not deferred: every CSS class used is declared in app.css (I caught myself inventing .field-optional/.field-hint and replaced them with the shared .muted); both tables in AdministrationMenu.razor balance at 5 th / 5 td / 5 data-label; .form-field textarea is width:100% under universal box-sizing: border-box, so scenario 16's 375px barrier cannot be breached by the new controls; and I repaired a blank line I'd introduced inside a /// block that would have been CS1587 under warnings-as-errors.

One finding, F-77: three files claim Describe() labels "the five event types §8.2's CHECK admits", and AdministrationMenu.razor names Stage 2's new types as two where the plan specifies three. A hand-maintained census of a mechanically derivable vocabulary, in triplicate — F-47's habit. All three now state the property without a number.

Predicted count: 1107 + 17 = 1124. Arithmetic on Slice 37's observed 1107, not an observation. §16.3 stays at 16.

I deliberately won't hand you a partial archive. The atomic-documentation rule is the thing that makes this project legible, and code without its spec edits is exactly what F-70 was. Files to DELETE: none. That one git add is the only untracked file — the gates walk git ls-files, so tree hygiene can't see it otherwise. No new directory; Migrations/ already globs *.sql as an EmbeddedResource.

The cut
Slice 37's Still open scoped 0004 as the whole item half, including three surfaces pulled forward. I cut between the item's own columns instead — Slice 37's own test one register lower. 0004 adds description and display_order, both NOT NULL with a DEFAULT, plus description_changed and reordered. No backfill, no form obligation, and because display_order defaults to 0, ORDER BY (display_order, name, identifier) is the name ordering this table has always had. Green by construction. menu_section_identifier and its three surfaces are 0005, paid on their own.

Descriptions aren't schema-only, though — authored, stored, logged, read back and displayed this slice, across all three administration surfaces. What guests don't get is the card layout, because a sentence inside a <select> option is the problem Stage 3 exists to fix, not a smaller version of the fix.

F-77
MenuEventLog, AdministrationMenu.razor and ManageMenuItem.razor all said "the five event types §8.2's CHECK admits" — and one of them named Stage 2's new types as two where the plan specifies three, omitting reordered, which this slice implements. Counts deleted rather than corrected: a corrected count goes stale again in 0005. No gate added, deliberately — the switch arms are their own census. The apparent contradiction with F-73 (where a count was kept) is recorded rather than left to be tripped over.

Verification, including where it caught me
Four things were wrong before packaging and are fixed:

The first §16.4 draft described four test classes in one paragraph with one count — unattributable, the exact finding Slice 37 hit. Split into four. Final state: sixteen counted paragraphs, every claim matching its file, zero ambiguity. The gate's floor moved from ten to sixteen with it (F-73's habit, second application).
CreateMenuItem.razor invented .field-optional and .field-hint. Neither exists in app.css. Both are now .muted; all thirteen classes verified declared.
Splitting a <para> left a bare blank line inside a /// block — CS1587 under warnings-as-errors.
My own balance walker mis-parsed $""" and reported three false failures, which is why untouched siblings are in the run as controls. Proven sensitive afterwards by three planted defects; the Razor walk needed the same treatment for => in attributes and for generics in @code — Slice 36's standing false report.
SpecificationVersionTests simulated (header 1.23, 24 entries descending); Markdown table gate simulated over 24 documents, 57 runs, zero problems; byte hygiene clean on all 22 files.

Predicted 1124 (1107 + 8 + 2 + 2 + 5). Arithmetic, not an observation.

Two honest gaps
No database ran 0004. Slice 37 had PostgreSQL 16 and measured its schema half; this environment had none, so the migration is reasoned about. The three things a red run could mean are named in BUILD_PROGRESS.md — chiefly whether DbUp's splitter survives the dollar-quoted DO block, since a broken splitter leaves valid SQL that simply does less, presenting as a green migration against a table with no constraints. That's what Run_NamesTheMenuItemEventCheckConstraints decides.

No browser rendered the two new forms on ManageMenuItem.razor. A red first run on scenario 16's 375px measurement there is informational.
